summary: Login page QA — negative and edge handling is solid; double-submit and input hygiene need fixes; positive login is blocked pending user sign-in.

findings.title: Double-click on Login fires two GraphQL auth requests
findings.repro: 1. Open http://localhost:4201/login  2. Enter a valid-format email and any password  3. Double-click Login within ~300 ms  4. Watch the Network panel
findings.actual: Two identical POST requests are sent to https://admin.f2finterview.com/graphql for one submit. The button stays enabled while the first request is in flight.
findings.expected: One authentication request per submit. The Login button is disabled from the first click until the request settles.
findings.fixDirection: Disable the submit control on click and re-enable it in the request's finally/completion handler; ignore submits while a request is pending.

findings.title: Password field uses autocomplete=new-password on a sign-in form
findings.repro: 1. Open /login  2. Inspect the email and password inputs in the DOM
findings.actual: The password input declares autocomplete="new-password", and the email input is type="text" with no autocomplete hint.
findings.expected: On a sign-in form the password input declares autocomplete="current-password" and the email input is type="email" autocomplete="username", so saved credentials are offered and mobile keyboards show the right layout.
findings.fixDirection: Set autocomplete="current-password" on the password field; set type="email" autocomplete="username" on the email field.

findings.title: No maximum length on email or password
findings.repro: 1. Open /login  2. Paste a 312-character email and a 502-character password  3. Submit
findings.actual: Both values are accepted and sent to the API unchanged; the form shows no length validation.
findings.expected: Client-side maximum lengths (e.g. 254 for email per RFC 5321, a documented bound for password) reject over-long input before a request is made.
findings.fixDirection: Add maxlength attributes and matching form-control validators; mirror the bounds server-side so the client is not the only check.

findings.title: Leading and trailing spaces in the email are not trimmed
findings.repro: 1. Open /login  2. Type "  user@example.com  " with surrounding spaces  3. Submit
findings.actual: The untrimmed value is validated and submitted, so a copy-paste with a trailing space reads as an invalid email.
findings.expected: The email is trimmed before validation and before the request, so surrounding whitespace does not change the outcome.
findings.fixDirection: Trim the email on blur and again before submit; keep the raw value only for display.

findings.title: Both inputs share name="inputTxt"
findings.repro: 1. Open /login  2. Inspect the name attribute on both inputs
findings.actual: The email and password inputs both use name="inputTxt", so they are indistinguishable to password managers, autofill, and any test selecting by name.
findings.expected: Each input has a distinct, meaningful name (email, password) matching its autocomplete role.
findings.fixDirection: Rename the inputs to email and password and update any bindings or selectors that relied on inputTxt.

findings.title: Development main.js is ~16 MB on a cold load
findings.repro: 1. Hard-reload http://localhost:4201/login with an empty cache  2. Read the transfer size of main.js in the Network panel
findings.actual: main.js transfers at roughly 16 MB cold, because this is an unoptimised ng serve development build.
findings.expected: A production build ships a bundle an order of magnitude smaller; this figure is not a production measurement and must be re-measured against a built artifact.
findings.fixDirection: Re-measure against ng build --configuration production before treating bundle size as a defect; if it remains large, budget it in angular.json.

whatWorksWell: Empty required fields keep Login disabled and show "This field is required"
An invalid email format shows "Please enter valid Email" and blocks submit
Wrong or unknown credentials stay on /login with an "Invalid login credentials" banner
The password visibility toggle switches the input between password and text
An XSS payload in the email field does not execute; it is treated as an invalid email
A SQLi-style password does not bypass authentication; the page stays on login with an error
The 375px mobile layout has no horizontal overflow and the form remains usable
fixOrder: EXP-1 — one auth request per submit (a duplicate login attempt is user-visible and can trip rate limiting)
EXP-3 — bound the input lengths on both client and server
EXP-2 — correct the autocomplete and input types so credential managers work
EXP-5 — give the inputs distinct names
EXP-4 — trim the email before validation
EXP-6 — re-measure the bundle against a production build before acting

recommendations.action: Guard the submit handler against concurrent requests, then re-run TC-16
Add maxlength bounds to both fields and mirror them server-side
Ask the user to sign in once so TC-1 (positive login) can be unblocked
Re-check security headers against the deployed environment, not ng serve

scope.objective: Check whether a first-time user can sign in to the admin console, and whether the login form behaves correctly when they get it wrong — bad password, unknown email, empty fields, pasted whitespace, and a slip of the mouse.
covered: The sign-in form at /login: email field, password field, password visibility toggle, Login button, and the Forgot Password link
Every way a sign-in can fail: wrong password, unknown email, empty fields, malformed email, and text pasted with surrounding spaces
The GraphQL authentication request the page sends, and the error message it returns
Hostile input in both fields: SQL-injection strings and an XSS payload
The form on a 375px-wide mobile screen, and with the keyboard alone
What the browser downloads on a first, uncached visit to the page
notCovered: Signing in successfully. Doing so needs real credentials, which a QA run must never enter on the user's behalf — so everything behind the login wall is untested.
Password reset beyond confirming the link navigates: no email was sent or received.
Security headers. This run hit a local development server, where they are absent by design; they must be re-checked against the deployed environment.
Rate limiting and account lockout after repeated failures, which would have locked the test account.
